body.statement: For every \(\mathfrak G\in\mathfrak E\), the value \(M_{\mathfrak G,\eta}(r)\) is attained by a globally honest randomized rule and equals the supremum of the Lagrange dual over finite nonnegative atomic coverage measures on the regions \(D_v\) and finite atomic probability measures on \(H_r\). Every finite atomic dual is a valid lower certificate. An increasing enumeration of finite atomic certificates with rational weights and rationally encoded real-algebraic support points converges upward to \(M_{\mathfrak G,\eta}(r)\), without a bounded-support premise.
body.justification: Attainment and dense atomic duality identify the exact object that the outward primal and dual programs must enclose.
body.gap: Goldenshluger, Juditsky, and Nemirovski establish compact-convex pairwise detector saddles, and Schafer and Stark approximate compact-parameter minimax expected size; neither treats globally honest finite-label rules over an unbounded fan.
body.consumer: CertGluePFL obtains valid lower endpoints without assuming that least-favorable mass is spatially tight.
body.proof_tex:
Put \(m=|\mathcal A|\), let \(\mu\) be Lebesgue measure on \(\mathbb R^d\), and represent a randomized rule by a vector \(p=(p_A)_{A\in\mathcal A}\) satisfying
\[
 p_A\geq 0,\qquad \sum_{A\in\mathcal A}p_A=1
 \quad\mu\text{-almost everywhere}.
\tag{1}
\]
Call the set of these vectors \(\mathscr K\).  This representation is exact because \(\mathcal A\) is finite.  We first establish compactness rather than impose it.

For \(j\geq1\), let \(B_j=[-j,j]^d\), and choose a countable orthonormal basis \((e_{jk})_{k\geq1}\) of \(L^2(B_j)\).  Since \(0\leq p_A\leq1\),
\[
 \|p_A\|_{L^2(B_j)}\leq \mu(B_j)^{1/2}.
\tag{2}
\]
Given a sequence in \(\mathscr K\), diagonal extraction over the countable triples \((A,j,k)\) makes every coefficient \(\langle p_A,e_{jk}\rangle_{L^2(B_j)}\) converge.  Bessel's inequality and (2) identify the limiting coefficients with an element \(p_A^{(j)}\in L^2(B_j)\), and the extracted sequence converges weakly to it.  The limits on nested boxes agree, because a test function on \(B_j\), extended by zero, is a test function on \(B_{j+1}\).  They therefore define a measurable function \(p_A\) on \(\mathbb R^d\).  For every nonnegative \(q\in L^2(B_j)\), weak convergence gives \(\int_{B_j}p_Aq\,d\mu\geq0\).  Taking \(q=(p_A)_-\), applying the same argument to \(1-p_A\), and testing \(\sum_Ap_A-1\) and its negative prove (1) for the limit.  The bounded differences of the countably many displayed coefficients define a metric for the coordinatewise local weak topology on the sets bounded by (2).  The diagonal argument proves sequential compactness in this metric, hence compactness of \(\mathscr K\).

For \(v\in V\), \(h\in D_v\), and \(g\in H_r\), define
\[
 c_{v,h}(p)=\int\phi_\Sigma(w-h)\sum_{A\ni v}p_A(w)\,dw,
 \qquad
 r_g(p)=\int\phi_\Sigma(w-g)\sum_A\ell(A)p_A(w)\,dw.
\tag{3}
\]
The positive definiteness of \(\Sigma\) makes each translated Gaussian density square integrable on every \(B_j\).  Local weak convergence therefore gives convergence of both integrals over \(B_j\).  The contribution outside \(B_j\) is bounded by the corresponding Gaussian tail for \(c_{v,h}\), and by \(D\) times that tail for \(r_g\).  Letting \(j\to\infty\) proves that every functional in (3) is continuous on \(\mathscr K\).

Consequently,
\[
 \mathscr K_\eta=
 \bigcap_{v\in V}\bigcap_{h\in D_v}
 \{p\in\mathscr K:c_{v,h}(p)\geq1-\eta\}
\tag{4}
\]
is compact.  It is nonempty because the rule reporting \(V\) surely belongs to it.  The map \(p\mapsto\sup_{g\in H_r}r_g(p)\) is a supremum of continuous functions and is therefore lower semicontinuous.  It attains its minimum on (4).  All Gaussian shifts with covariance \(\Sigma\succ0\) are equivalent to Lebesgue measure, so changing the finitely many coordinates on one common null set turns the minimizing representative into a Markov kernel valid for every mean.  This proves primal attainment.

We next derive the dual and its exact finite-atomic exhaustion.  Let
\[
 \alpha_v=\sum_{j=1}^{J_v}a_{vj}\delta_{h_{vj}},
 \quad a_{vj}\geq0,\quad h_{vj}\in D_v,
 \qquad
 \beta=\sum_{i=1}^{I}b_i\delta_{g_i},
 \quad b_i\geq0,\quad \sum_i b_i=1,\quad g_i\in H_r,
\tag{5}
\]
and set
\[
 a_v(w)=\int\phi_\Sigma(w-h)\,\alpha_v(dh),
 \qquad
 b(w)=\int\phi_\Sigma(w-g)\,\beta(dg).
\tag{6}
\]
The Lagrangian for the risk epigraph and the coverage inequalities is
\[
 (1-\eta)\sum_v\alpha_v(D_v)
 +\int\sum_{A\subseteq V}p_A(w)
 \left\{b(w)\ell(A)-\sum_{v\in A}a_v(w)\right\}dw.
\tag{7}
\]
At each \(w\), (1) ranges over a finite simplex.  Choosing the first minimizing action in a fixed enumeration is measurable, so minimization of (7) gives
\[
 \mathcal D(\alpha,\beta)
 =(1-\eta)\sum_v\alpha_v(D_v)
 +\int\min_{A\subseteq V}
 \left\{b(w)\ell(A)-\sum_{v\in A}a_v(w)\right\}dw.
\tag{8}
\]
For every \(p\in\mathscr K_\eta\), Tonelli's theorem applies to the nonnegative Gaussian mixtures in (6), and (3), (5), and (7) imply
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathcal D(\alpha,\beta)
 &\leq \sum_i b_i r_{g_i}(p)
   +\sum_{v,j}a_{vj}\{(1-\eta)-c_{v,h_{vj}}(p)\}\\
 &\leq \sup_{g\in H_r}r_g(p).
 \end{aligned}
\tag{9}
\]
Thus every finite atomic dual is a valid lower certificate.

To prove exhaustion, fix \(t<M_{\mathfrak G,\eta}(r)\).  The open sets
\[
 \{p:r_g(p)>t\},\quad g\in H_r,
 \qquad
 \{p:c_{v,h}(p)<1-\eta\},\quad v\in V,\ h\in D_v,
\tag{10}
\]
cover \(\mathscr K\): an honest rule has supremum risk at least \(M_{\mathfrak G,\eta}(r)>t\), while a nonhonest rule violates one inequality in (4).  Compactness gives a finite subcover with risk points \(g_1,\ldots,g_I\) and coverage points \((v_j,h_j)\), \(j=1,\ldots,J\).  The compact convex set
\[
 Y=\left\{
 \bigl((r_{g_i}(p)-t)_{i\leq I},
 ((1-\eta)-c_{v_j,h_j}(p))_{j\leq J}\bigr):p\in\mathscr K
 \right\}
\tag{11}
\]
is disjoint from the closed negative orthant.  Let \((y_*,z_*)\) minimize \(\|y-z\|_2^2\) over \(y\in Y\) and \(z\) in that orthant, and put \(n=y_*-z_*\).  Coordinatewise projection gives \(n\geq0\), \(n'z_*=0\), and \(n'y_*=\|n\|_2^2>0\).  The first-order inequality for minimization over the convex set \(Y\) gives \(n'y\geq n'y_*\) for every \(y\in Y\).  Hence there are \(\gamma_i,\zeta_j\geq0\), not all zero, and \(q>0\) such that
\[
 \sum_i\gamma_i\{r_{g_i}(p)-t\}
 +\sum_j\zeta_j\{(1-\eta)-c_{v_j,h_j}(p)\}
 \geq q
 \quad\text{for every }p\in\mathscr K.
\tag{12}
\]
For the rule reporting \(V\), every coverage deficit in (12) equals \(-\eta\).  Therefore \(G=\sum_i\gamma_i>0\).  Set \(b_i=\gamma_i/G\), and assign mass \(a_j=\zeta_j/G\) to the coverage atom \((v_j,h_j)\).  Dividing (12) by \(G\), taking the infimum over \(p\in\mathscr K\), and using (8) yield
\[
 \mathcal D(\alpha,\beta)\geq t+q/G>t.
\tag{13}
\]
Combining (9) and (13), and then taking \(t\uparrow M_{\mathfrak G,\eta}(r)\), proves
\[
 M_{\mathfrak G,\eta}(r)
 =\sup_{\alpha,\beta\ {
m finite\ atomic}}\mathcal D(\alpha,\beta).
\tag{14}
\]

It remains to justify the asserted effective restriction on atoms.  Each \(D_v\) is a finite union of rational polyhedra.  Membership in \(H_r\) is a finite Boolean combination of membership in those polyhedra and inequalities
\[
 \inf_{x:Ax\leq b}(h-x)'\Sigma^{-1}(h-x)\geq r^2.
\tag{15}
\]
For every active set of the quadratic program in (15), its primal feasibility, stationarity, complementary slackness, and the displayed value inequality are polynomial equalities and inequalities with rational coefficients.  Taking the finite disjunction over active sets and eliminating the primal and multiplier variables by recursive polynomial sign decomposition gives a rational semialgebraic description of \(H_r\).  The same sign-decomposition recursion decides whether a rational box meets any one of these sets and, when it does, isolates a real-algebraic sample point.  Enumerating rational boxes therefore gives a dense, effectively enumerable family of rationally encoded real-algebraic points in every \(D_v\) and in \(H_r\), including their lower-dimensional components.

If \(x_n\to x\), then translated Gaussian densities converge pointwise, and
\[
 \int|\phi_\Sigma(w-x_n)-\phi_\Sigma(w-x)|\,dw
 =2-2\int\min\{\phi_\Sigma(w-x_n),\phi_\Sigma(w-x)\}\,dw
 \longrightarrow0
\tag{16}
\]
by dominated convergence.  Perturbing finitely many support points within their respective sets, and perturbing the weights to nonnegative rationals while preserving \(\sum_i b_i=1\), consequently makes all mixtures in (6) converge in \(L^1\).  Since
\[
 \left|\min_Ax_A-\min_Ay_A\right|\leq\max_A|x_A-y_A|,
\tag{17}
\]
the dual values in (8) converge as well.  Thus rational weights and rationally encoded real-algebraic support points are dense among finite atomic certificates.

Finally, each such dual value is a computable real.  On a rational box, the finitely many Gaussian mixtures have computable uniform derivative bounds, so interval Riemann sums give convergent rational lower and upper bounds for the finite minimum in (8).  Outside the box, the absolute integrand is bounded by \(Db(w)+\sum_va_v(w)\), and the finitely many Gaussian tails have effective outward rational bounds.  Enumerate all atomic certificates and dovetail these two-sided enclosures.  Maintain one certificate and replace it only by a candidate whose certified lower enclosure exceeds the current certificate's certified upper enclosure, choosing at each stage the candidate with the largest certified lower endpoint.  Exact certificate values then increase.  If their limit were below the supremum in (14), a previously enumerated certificate separated from that limit would eventually have its strict advantage certified, a contradiction.  The resulting increasing sequence converges upward to \(M_{\mathfrak G,\eta}(r)\), and no bounded-support premise has been used.
